flashcards.q: Interpretability vs explainability — one sentence each.
flashcards.a: Interpretability is a property of the MODEL: how far its mechanism is human-understandable (global, intrinsic). Explainability is a property of an ACCOUNT OF ONE OUTPUT: why this input produced this output (local, usually post-hoc). For LLM systems interpretability is a research programme; explainability is an engineering deliverable made of traces and citations.

flashcards.q: The four-layer explanation stack. Which layers do you ship?
flashcards.a: L1 mechanistic (circuits, attribution graphs) = research only. L2 model-behavioural (SHAP/LIME/IG) = tabular components only. L3 SYSTEM TRACE = ship it, faithful by construction. L4 user rationale + citations = ship it, derived from L3 only. Chain-of-thought lives at L4, NOT L3.

flashcards.q: Faithfulness vs plausibility, and why the distinction is a product risk.
flashcards.a: Faithfulness = the explanation matches the process that produced the output. Plausibility = a human finds it convincing. They are independent axes and only plausibility is visible to users, PMs, and human raters, so RLHF and A/B tests optimise the wrong one. Plausible explanations raise acceptance of WRONG outputs.

flashcards.q: Cite the CoT unfaithfulness evidence with numbers.
flashcards.a: Turpin et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.04388): biasing features drop accuracy up to 36% on 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks while CoT rationalises without mentioning the bias. Anthropic 2025 (arXiv:2505.05410): hint-verbalisation faithfulness 25% Claude 3.7 Sonnet / 39% DeepSeek R1, falling to 20% / 29% on harmful hints and worsening as tasks get harder. Arcuschin 2025 (arXiv:2503.08679): unfaithful on natural prompts with NO injected bias.

flashcards.q: Why exactly is chain-of-thought not an explanation of the computation?
flashcards.a: The CoT tokens are sampled autoregressively from the same distribution as the answer. Nothing in training ties them to the forward-pass computation that determined the answer, and RLHF rewards them for being convincing. Keep two claims separate: CoT is often causally load-bearing (erase it, accuracy drops) but is NOT a faithful description of the computation (25-39% on the standard test).

flashcards.q: Why is a trace faithful when CoT is not?
flashcards.a: Because emitting a trace is a DIFFERENT ACT from doing the work. A retrieval span is written by the retrieval code as a side effect; it cannot rationalise because it is not generated by a policy optimised for plausibility. A log is a record; a chain of thought is a story about a record.

flashcards.q: Give the arithmetic that rules SHAP out for LLMs.
flashcards.a: Exact Shapley = 2^|F| coalitions. KernelSHAP needs roughly 2|F| + 2048 samples, so ~3k forward passes per explained output at 512 tokens, and real prompts are 10-50k tokens. Plus: tokens are correlated so the marginal reference puts mass off-manifold, and SHAP explains a SCALAR while an LLM emits a sequence.

flashcards.q: Where does SHAP still belong, and what is TreeSHAP's complexity?
flashcards.a: On the non-generative models in the pipeline: the reranker's feature-based scorer, CTR or fraud models, the router. TreeSHAP is exact and O(T·L·D²) for T trees, L leaves, D depth, so it is cheap there. The point is scoping, not dismissal.

flashcards.q: Name LIME's two known failure modes.
flashcards.a: 1) Seed instability: different random perturbation samples give different top-k features for the same input, so you must run it n>=10 times and report only stable features. 2) Kernel width sigma is a free parameter with no principled default and no cross-validation objective, so changing it changes which features look important.

flashcards.q: Why does integrated gradients not transfer to text?
flashcards.a: IG needs a neutral baseline x'. For images, all-black works. For text there is none: the zero embedding is off-manifold, [PAD] and [MASK] carry learned meaning, and the baseline choice can flip attribution signs. It also needs white-box gradients (20-300 Riemann steps; check completeness sum ≈ f(x)−f(x') within ~5%), which you do not have for API models.

flashcards.q: The honesty ladder of LLM attribution: what can you claim, and at what cost?
flashcards.a: Provenance ('these tokens were in context') cost ~0, always on. NLI entailment ('this passage entails this sentence') one small-model call per sentence. Leave-one-out ('removing this chunk changes the answer') k+1 generations, audit path. SHAP on tabular: 100s-1000s of evals, batch. Attribution graphs: research. CoT: cost ~0 and it is the only rung that is a lie.

flashcards.q: Chunk occlusion says a chunk has zero influence. What do you conclude?
flashcards.a: Only that it was not NECESSARY given everything else present. Either it was irrelevant, or the fact was redundantly available in another chunk or in the weights. Occlusion measures necessity, not sufficiency. To disambiguate, run sufficiency (that chunk alone) and a closed-book baseline: three numbers are interpretable, one is not. Cost at k=10 is ~22 generation calls, so it is an audit-path technique.

flashcards.q: What must a trace pin for an explanation to be replayable?
flashcards.a: model@version, prompt template@version, tool schema version, index snapshot id. Plus retrieval query after rewrite, top-k doc ids with scores, rerank input/output order, tool arguments, guardrail verdicts, decision branches with budget remaining. Store result HASH + bounded prefix, not the full payload.

flashcards.q: Model card vs system card, and who owns each?
flashcards.a: Model card (Mitchell et al. 2019) documents the trained artefact: intended and out-of-scope use, training data summary, evaluation disaggregated by subgroup, caveats. For a frontier API model it is the provider's; for your fine-tune it is yours. System card documents the deployed composition — model + retrieval + tools + guardrails + human oversight — and the failure modes that only exist in the composition. That one is always yours.

flashcards.q: What the EU AI Act actually requires on explanation, and when.
flashcards.a: Not 'explainable models'. Article 13 requires transparency sufficient for deployers to interpret and use output appropriately; Article 14 requires oversight persons be able to correctly interpret output and override it. High-risk obligations plus Article 50 transparency and the GPAI documentation stack (internal docs, public model card, deployer package, training-data summary) apply from 2 August 2026, with penalties to €35M or 6-7% of global turnover depending on provision.

flashcards.q: Why is an explanation an attack surface, and what is the pattern?
flashcards.a: It leaks system-prompt structure, corpus composition, and threshold behaviour, so for adversarial decisions (fraud, abuse, pricing, moderation) a faithful explanation is a specification for evading the system. Pattern: two tiers — full trace to the internal reviewer, a fixed audited reason code plus an appeal route to the subject. No scores, no feature ordering, no 'you were 0.02 away', and rate-limit the endpoint since perturbed repeat queries are model extraction.

flashcards.q: How do you test whether an explanation actually helps?
flashcards.a: Error injection on the HUMANS, not the model: take N real outputs, corrupt a specific claim in a random half, show explanation and no-explanation arms to reviewers, and measure detection rate and time-to-decision. If detection does not improve, the explanation is decoration. Almost nobody runs this eval.

flashcards.q: Attention weights as explanation — the 2019 verdict.
flashcards.a: No. Jain & Wallace (NAACL 2019) constructed adversarial attention distributions producing the same prediction with completely different weights, so attention is not identifiable as the explanation. Wiegreffe & Pinter (EMNLP 2019) pushed back on the strongest reading without restoring it. In deep transformers it is worse: layer-7 attention is over representations that already mixed everything. Rollout/flow help coarse localisation and are still not causal.

flashcards.q: Where is mechanistic interpretability today, operationally?
flashcards.a: Anthropic's circuit tracing with cross-layer transcoders builds attribution graphs and was open-sourced as circuit-tracer in May 2025; MIT Tech Review named mech interp a 2026 Breakthrough Technology. Legitimate uses today: post-incident forensics on open-weights models you control, and safety research. Not a production explanation path — you need a transcoder per model and graph construction costs orders of magnitude more than the generation it explains.

flashcards.q: Verification instead of explanation — the two managed examples and what they buy.
flashcards.a: Bedrock Guardrails contextual grounding filters over 75% of hallucinated responses on RAG and summarisation by checking output against source. Bedrock Automated Reasoning checks (GA Aug 2025) encode a policy into formal logic and validate outputs with claimed up to 99% accuracy. Note precisely what that is: a soundness claim over a FORMALISED policy, not an explanation, and it only exists where someone did the formalisation.
